label: PF Backlog 536
title: Backlog dependency guard + BLOCKS direction: drop self/unknown/parent-epic/cyclic deps at the writer
body:
## Problem
AI grooming produced dependencies that deadlocked the backlog. Two defects:
1. Scheduler read BLOCKS backwards: 'A BLOCKS B' means B waits on A, but eligible() treated it as A waits on B -> false cycles (0387<->0388, 0386<->0407, 0397<->0398/0399).
2. No guard at the dependency writer: items could be stored with a self-dep, an unknown id (pfssot-p11-adapters), a child depending on its own parent EPIC (0403/0404/0405 -> 0391; 0374 -> 0360), or a REQUIRES cycle -> permanent deadlock.

## Root cause (5-Why)
1. Backlog deadlocked. 2. Items waited on their own parent epic / on unknown ids, and BLOCKS was read as the inverse edge. 3. set_dependencies stored any edge; eligible() did not interpret direction. 4. No validation at the single writer and no cycle test. 5. No guard test asserted these are rejected.

## Fix
- eligible(): REQUIRES X = this item waits on X; BLOCKS X = X waits on this (does NOT block this); RELATED advisory. (blocking = REQUIRES only, + flat deps/blocked_by back-compat.)
- set_dependencies(): fail-safe guard drops (never stores) self / unknown / parent-epic / REQUIRES-cycle edges; keeps valid ones; prints dropped ids. Single writer -> holds for AI and human alike.

## In scope
- core/scheduler.py direction handling; core/backlog.py set_dependencies guard
- tests

## Out of scope
- AI dep inference quality; required_state semantics

## Acceptance
- BLOCKS edge does not block the item itself; REQUIRES on an open item blocks; completed deps are met.
- self/unknown/parent-epic/cycle deps are dropped; valid edges kept.
- No cycles in the live backlog after the guard; roots eligible.
